headline: OCEANAGOLD Q2: $647M REVENUE, $130M FREE CASH FLOW, ZERO DEBT — 138,800 Oz At $4,433 Realized; AISC $2,151/oz; Haile Exploration Hits; H2 Guidance On Track (TSX: OGC)
snippet: OceanaGold Corp. (TSX: OGC) reported Q2 2026 results August 6, posting production of 138,800 ounces of gold and 2,700 tonnes of copper — up 7% quarter-on-quarter — at an average realized gold price of $4,433 per ounce. Revenue totalled $647 million with free cash flow of $130 million; the company ended the quarter with $655 million cash and zero debt, giving management significant balance-sheet flexibility. All-in sustaining cost was $2,151 per ounce, expected to decrease in H2 as production ramps and sustaining capital moderates. The company also released additional high-grade exploration results at Haile in South Carolina supporting ongoing resource growth at its flagship operation. OGC is on track to achieve full-year production, cost, and capital guidance.

headline: MCEWEN Q2: GREY FOX HITS 97.7 g/t AU OVER 4.4m, 64.8 g/t Over 3.3m — Net Income Triples To $9.6M; New Stock Mine Nearing Production In Timmins (TSX: MUX)
snippet: McEwen Mining Inc. (TSX: MUX) reported Q2 2026 net income of $9.6 million ($0.16 per share) on August 6 — a 220% increase from $3.0 million ($0.06/share) in Q2 2025 — as exploration results across all sites continued to drive resource growth. Grey Fox highlights include 97.7 g/t gold over 4.4 metres, 64.8 g/t Au over 3.3 metres, and 32.5 g/t Au over 5.2 metres, with a June 8 Mineral Reserve Estimate confirming 980,300 Probable ounces at the project. Separately, the New Stock Mine in Timmins, Ontario is nearing production with an extended mine life, adding a near-term production catalyst to McEwen's gold portfolio. McEwen Copper's Los Azules project in Argentina continues to advance in parallel.

headline: COPPER FOX CONFIRMS 279m PORPHYRY AT MINERAL MOUNTAIN — Up To 1.48% Cu, 0.313% Mo; Bornite At Depth Points To Hotter Core; 25km From Rio Tinto's Giant Resolution (TSX-V: CUU)
snippet: Copper Fox Metals Inc. (TSX-V: CUU) reported August 6, 2026 that diamond drillhole MM-02-2025 at its 100%-owned Mineral Mountain porphyry copper project in Arizona intersected a 278.97-metre interval (1,379–1,657.97m depth) of porphyry-style mineralization grading locally up to 1.48% copper, 0.313% molybdenum, plus silver and rhenium values that increase progressively with depth. The hole cut strong phyllic alteration, cross-cutting sulphide vein assemblages, and bornite rimming chalcopyrite — geochemical vectors pointing toward a hotter potassic core interpreted to lie deeper than current drilling. Mineral Mountain sits 25 kilometres southwest of Rio Tinto and BHP's Resolution deposit — one of the largest undeveloped porphyry copper systems in North America — and 20 kilometres northeast of the recently commissioned Florence copper mine, placing it within a proven copper-productive northeast-trending belt.

headline: VAL-D'OR MINING HITS 3.08 g/t AU OVER 84m AT PERESTROIKA — 12,477m Phase II Complete In Quebec; Phase III Launched As Gold Corridor Expands Along Strike (TSX-V: VZZ)
snippet: Val-d'Or Mining Corporation (TSX-V: VZZ, OTCQB: VDOMF) reported August 5, 2026 initial analytical results from 25 NQ diamond drillholes (PE-26-021 through PE-26-045), totalling 12,477 metres completed during the winter 2026 phase at the Perestroika Prospect, Quebec — an option project from Eldorado Gold. Standout hole PE-26-027 returned 3.08 g/t gold over 84.0 metres (75.0–159.0m depth), one of the widest bulk-grade gold intervals drilled at the project to date; PE-26-030 returned 3.07 g/t Au over 21.3 metres at 255.7–277.0m, confirming the corridor extends at depth. Multiple mineralized intervals of altered felsic dykes hosting quartz-ankerite veins were identified across the program, and Phase III drilling has now commenced to chase strike extensions of the confirmed high-grade gold corridor.

headline: NIOB CUTS RARE EARTH PEGMATITE IN ALL 8 BARDY DRILL HOLES — 75% REE Hit Rate; Allanite + Parisite Confirmed; Assays At SGS Canada; Quebec Critical Minerals (CSE: NIOB)
snippet: North American Niobium and Critical Minerals Corp. (CSE: NIOB) announced August 4, 2026 that its 2026 drill campaign at the Bardy Property in Quebec's Grenville Province delivered a 100% hit rate for target pegmatite dykes across all eight holes (1,554 metres total), with rare earth-bearing minerals — principally allanite, with parisite confirmed in hole BBY-2026-001 and apatite/possible monazite locally — identified visually in six of the eight holes. The strongest visual mineralization was in BBY-2026-006, which cut an eight-metre syenitic pegmatite with coarse allanite up to two centimetres wide. All core has been submitted to SGS Canada in Val-d'Or for full assay testing. NIOB's radon-targeting approach — which produced the 100% pegmatite and 75% rare earth hit rate — validates a repeatable drill-targeting method for the Bardy and Blanchette rare earth prospects, in a region with no existing Canadian rare earth production.

headline: EVOLUTION MINING TAKES 9.9% STAKE IN ARIZONA GOLD & SILVER — C$12M Strategic Placement At $0.80; 90% Of Proceeds For Philadelphia Project, Oatman District (TSX-V: AZS)
source_name: Investing News Network / Arizona Gold & Silver
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX-V: AZS) announced August 4, 2026 that Evolution Mining Gold Operations Ltd. — the gold mining arm of ASX-listed Evolution Mining, one of Australia's largest gold producers — has agreed to acquire 15,056,004 units at C$0.80 per unit for approximately C$12 million in a non-brokered strategic private placement, gaining a 9.9% equity stake on closing. Each unit includes one common share and one-half warrant exercisable at C$1.00 over three years; deal remains subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval. At least 90% of proceeds (~C$10.8 million) will be directed to accelerating exploration at the Philadelphia Gold-Silver Project in Arizona's historic Oatman Mining District — a prolific epithermal gold district with over 1.8 million ounces of historical production. The strategic backing by a multi-billion-dollar Australian gold producer provides both capital credibility and a potential future acquirer signal for the TSX-V junior.

headline: SILVER MINE CASH FLOW SURGES 336%, REVENUE JUMPS 149% IN Q2 — Endeavour Silver Delivers Proof That $60 Silver Unlocks Massive Operating Leverage Across The Sector (NYSE: EXK)
snippet: Streetwise Reports' August 5, 2026 analysis of silver producers' Q2 2026 results illustrates the operating leverage now visible across the primary silver sector: at Endeavour Silver (NYSE: EXK), revenue jumped 149% year-on-year to US$212.1 million as Terronera mine reached full production and Kolpa contributed for the first time, while mine operating cash flow before taxes surged 336% to US$99.9 million. Net earnings flipped from a US$20.5 million loss in Q2 2025 to a US$66.5 million profit. The piece contextualises these results sector-wide: at silver above $60, companies that built capacity during the bear market are delivering exponential cash flow conversion — at a fixed $20/oz AISC, the tripling of silver price from $20 to $60 produces roughly a tripling of mine-level profit per ounce with no incremental capital required, a leverage dynamic that static revenue growth numbers significantly understate.

headline: URANIUM JUNIORS DOWN 7.4% IN H1 AS TERM PRICE HITS 18-YEAR HIGH $94/LB — Spot/Equity Divergence Signals Structural Setup For Catch-Up Trade; URNJ +3% Tuesday
snippet: A structural divergence is building in uranium markets: long-term contract prices have climbed to US$94 per pound — the highest since 2008 — while spot uranium consolidates near US$85–87, and junior uranium mining equities actually fell 3.9% in H1 2026 (juniors specifically down 7.4%) even as those term prices climbed. The divergence reflects that equity markets price spot momentum while term markets price the structural supply deficit — a gap that historically resolves by equities catching up to the term price signal rather than term prices reverting lower. The Industry Spread analysis cites Cameco's confirmed 28-million-pound annual contracted deliveries over the next five years and AI hyperscaler data-centre nuclear demand as the fundamentals that make the H1 equity underperformance a potential entry window. The Sprott Junior Uranium Miners ETF (URNJ) finished up 3.04% on August 4, trading 1.2 times its typical volume — an early technical signal of renewed interest in the lagging junior cohort.

headline: MONEY METALS: GOLD CAUGHT BETWEEN WAR PREMIUM AND FED POLICY — Geopolitical Tailwinds Vs. Sticky Inflation; NFP The Swing Factor For Whether $4,300 Holds
snippet: A Money Metals Exchange analysis published August 4, 2026 framed the current gold and silver rally as a tug-of-war between escalating Middle East geopolitical tension — structurally bullish as investors seek safety and inflation protection — and sticky core inflation, elevated Treasury yields, and a firm US dollar acting as headwinds against a sustained breakout above $4,300. The article notes that gold is navigating a more complex macro environment than 2025's record-run, when the inflationary impulse and geopolitical risk were aligned in the same direction, and argues that Thursday's Non-Farm Payrolls is the clearest near-term signal of which force dominates. For mining investors, Money Metals argues the most interesting asymmetry sits in low-AISC producers whose margins are expanding dramatically regardless of whether the macro swing goes to $4,100 or $4,500 — because the structural gold floor is now fundamentally higher than 18 months ago.

headline: GOLD SET FOR BIGGEST WEEKLY JUMP IN 20 MONTHS ON HAVEN DEMAND — 6% Week Driven By Hormuz + ADP Miss; Why This Rally Is More Structural Than A Geopolitical Spike (GoldSeek)
snippet: GoldSeek reported August 5, 2026 that gold was on track for its biggest weekly percentage gain in 20 months — a move confirmed by Thursday's price near $4,278, up nearly 6% on the week — driven by the partial Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor deal, the ADP employment miss (44K vs. 70K), and a weakening US dollar. The analysis distinguishes the current haven demand from the type seen in Q1 2025: rather than pure fear-driven buying, this week's rally reflects a fundamental repricing of inflation expectations lower as energy costs ease with oil prices falling, which is historically more durable for gold's trend than short-term geopolitical spikes. For junior gold stocks, GoldSeek argues that $4,250 gold with easing inflation signals is operationally better than $5,000 gold with energy-driven inflation — because fuel and materials costs for mine operators move directly with oil prices that are now turning favourable.
